questions: Should the underscores replace every single space character, or only those that are not part of a run of more than two consecutive spaces?
When a run of more than two consecutive spaces is found, does "mark all consecutive spaces with -" mean replace each space in that run with a hyphen, or replace the entire run with a single hyphen?
If a run of exactly two consecutive spaces occurs, are those spaces replaced with underscores, left unchanged, or handled differently?
How should leading and trailing spaces in the input string be treated—are they subject to the same replacement/marking rules as interior spaces?
Must the function preserve other whitespace characters (e.g., tabs, newlines) unchanged, or should they be treated like spaces for replacement or marking?
Is the function expected to return a new string, modify the input in place (if mutable), or both, and what should be the exact return type?
Should the function raise an exception, return a special value, or silently handle non‑string inputs (e.g., None, integers)?
In the case of overlapping rules (e.g., a run of three spaces where the first two could be considered a separate pair), which rule takes precedence—underscore replacement or hyphen marking?
answers: Underscores replace every single space that is not part of a run longer than 2; runs longer than 2 are replaced with a single hyphen instead.
It means the entire run is replaced with a single hyphen, not each individual space.
A run of exactly two consecutive spaces is replaced with underscores (one underscore per space), not left unchanged.
Not applicable -- leading/trailing spaces follow the same general rule (underscore for runs of ≤2, hyphen for runs >2); no special-casing is described.
Not applicable -- only literal space characters are considered; other whitespace like tabs/newlines are left untouched.
Not applicable -- the function returns a new string; it does not mutate an input string in place (strings are immutable).
Not applicable -- input is guaranteed to be a string; no exception handling for other types is specified.
Runs are counted by their total consecutive length, not split into pairs -- a run of three is simply length 3 and gets a single hyphen, with no separate 'first two' pairing.
